issues.body: `paired_ids` is defined solely by the presence of token rows. Outcome grading then uses `answers.get(...)`, so a missing answer becomes `None` instead of blocking the verdict. For citations, only arm-side instrumentation is required; therefore a run with all token pairs, arm answers/records, and no baseline answers can remain `honest=true`, with the missing baselines graded as zero and the arm potentially producing a statistically significant `outcome_win` and `recommend_adopt=true`. This contradicts the stated requirement that every paired task have complete evidence and can positively bias the adoption decision. The current incomplete-pair test removes token rows, so it does not exercise this path.
issues.fix_hint: Require both `(task, base)` and `(task, arm)` to be present in `answers` (and any required records) for every relevant task; report missing answer pairs as a blocking reason rather than grading them as `None`. Add a refusal-path test that keeps all token pairs but removes one or all baseline answer entries and asserts `honest == false` and `recommend_adopt == false`.
issues.title: Missing baseline answers can still yield an honest adoption verdict

verdict.summary: The refusal-path tests pass, but the analyzer does not require a complete pair of answer records before treating a task as paired. Since missing answers are silently graded via `None`, incomplete experimental evidence can still produce an honest adoption verdict. This violates the pre-registration's completeness requirement and needs a real answer-pair guard plus a regression test.
